newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tung says Hong Kong budget prudent, balanced.
newsitem.headline: Tung says Hong Kong budget prudent, balanced.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader said on Tuesday the budget that will straddle the territory's handover to Chinese rule appeared "prudent".
"It is a very prudent budget," Tung Chee-hwa, who will become Hong Kong's Chief Executive after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, told reporters.
Hong Kong's last budget drawn up under British rule represents one aspect of the handover which appears to have aroused little controversy.
Tung said he had been briefed by Financial Secretary Donald Tsang, who will unveil the budget for the year starting April 1 to the territory's legislature on Wednesday.
"It is made consistent with the Basic Law, looking for a balance in the budget and also looking for expenditure not exceeding growth of our economy...so it is a well thought out budget," Tung said.
The Basic Law is Hong Kong's future China-drawn constitution. Since the budget straddles the British colony's June handover to Chinese sovereignty, Beijing was intimately involved in drawing it up.
Raymond Chi'en, a member of Governor Chris Patten's Executive Council which was also briefed by Tsang, hinted that the budget would be conservative.
"I think no surprises (in the budget) is again a tradition of Hong Kong," he told reporters.
Hong Kong has long kept to a policy of keeping growth in expenditure within the trend growth rate of the economy. Hefty budget surpluses are another tradition.
